newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico not obliged to aid in financing projects.
newsitem.headline: Mexico not obliged to aid in financing projects.

text.p: Mexican Energy Minister Jesus Reyes Heroles said Thursday the country will not intervene and help companies obtain financing for large domestic projects.

"When we talk about a private project, it means the risks and profits are taken on by the individual companies," Reyes told reporters at the inauguration here of the "Opportunities in Natural Gas Distribution" conference.

Financing problems are said to be tricky for larger energy projects, such as the approximately $400 million construction of thermoelectric power plant Merida III in Yucatan. Builders of the site AES * and Mitsui * and Mexican * are said to be still searching for financing sources.

Analysts and industry officials say private companies are reluctant to put themselves on the line for financing and international lenders are wary of Mexico's sovereign risk and its first steps toward private energy generation.

"Evidently financing will have to be obtained by winning companies and will have to be from international banks, because they are such large quantities and long terms and the Mexican financial markets don't have these characteristics," Reyes said, refering to the larger construction projects.

Financing problems are said to be holding up the approximately $400 million construction of thermoelectric power plant Merida III in Yucatan. Builders of the site, AES * and Mitsui * and Mexican *, are still searching for financing sources.

A sticking point for the separate, about $400 million Merida pipeline contract is the fact that supply and demand both depend on the state, analysts said. State oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) controls supply and the state monopoly Federal Electricity Commission (CFE) will be the region's top natural gas users.

Reyes said the government will offer regulatory support and its commitment to the projects. He said smaller natural gas distribution contracts, typically a $25-50 million investment, have not had financing difficulty.

Mexico did intervene to help the winners of the Northeast Railway concession earlier this year after the companies were unable to obtain international financing for their $1.4 billion bid. The government holds a 33.5 percent stake in the rail with Transportacion Maritima Mexicana and Kansas City Southern Industries.

Investment for distributing natural gas in Mexico City is expected to be about $900 billion. Total spending develop natural gas infrastructure in sites to be auctioned in coming months, Mexico City, La Laguna, Monterrey, Bajio, Tijuana and Queretaro, is estimated at $1.259 billion, Reyes said.
